A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same research work and contain readable main text, figures, tables, equations, and Appendices A–C. The complete material supports a reliable comparison.

before.justification: v2 reports original ProsQA experiments, attention and latent-representation analyses, a supervision comparison, and representation results across three random seeds.

after.justification: v3 retains these original empirical results in Section 5 and Appendix C, including benchmark accuracy and analyses of trained models.

M1.justification: The two-layer transformer construction, attention chooser, superposition updates, MLP filtering, and final readout remain unchanged. The COCONUT and COCONUT-BFS training procedures are also retained.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same ProsQA subset with solutions requiring 3–4 reasoning hops. No datasets, domains, tasks, or test scenarios are added or removed.

E2.justification: Figure 4 retains CoT, the larger CoT* model, and No CoT as comparators; Section 5.4 retains COCONUT-BFS. The newly cited Gozeten et al. work is discussed theoretically, not evaluated as a baseline.

E3.justification: The model configurations, optimizer settings, 300-epoch curriculum, stage mixing, and analysis procedures are unchanged. Table 4 retains the same 14,785 training, 257 validation, and 419 test problems.

E4.justification: Both versions contain the same attention and representation analyses in Section 5.3, optimal-path versus frontier supervision comparison in Section 5.4, and representation-stability analysis in Appendix C.2.

E5.justification: Table 1 retains test-set means and standard deviations. Appendix C.2 and Table 5 retain the same three-random-seed analysis and per-run inner products, with no changes to uncertainty-reporting practices.

E6.justification: Figure 4 and Section 5.2 retain near-perfect COCONUT accuracy, approximately 75% for CoT and No CoT, and 83% for CoT*. The attention scores, representation plots, three-seed values, and COCONUT-BFS findings are unchanged.

T1.justification: The definitions, lemmas, Theorem 1, and Appendix B constructions and proofs remain mathematically unchanged, including the RoPE extension. Wording and appendix-reference edits do not alter the formal content.

C1.justification: Both versions retain the two-layer, D-step graph-reachability claim, comparison with the best-known O(n²) discrete-CoT construction, and emergence-of-superposition claim. The added related-work comparison contextualizes the existing contribution.

C2.justification: The explanations of frontier and optimal-node preferences, interpretation of COCONUT-BFS, and discussion of buffer spaces remain unchanged. The conclusion retains the open questions about discrete-CoT lower bounds, training dynamics, and broader applicability.

D1.justification: The code link, implementation and training details, and dataset statistics are retained. Appendix C.3 still reports approximately 24 hours on two Nvidia A100 80GB GPUs per COCONUT run.

R1.justification: Section 1.1 adds Gozeten et al. (2025) and its reference entry. The new passage presents arithmetic-domain superposition as complementary and contrasts that work's exponential embedding dimension with this construction's linear dimension, providing a limited positioning update.

P1.justification: v3 standardizes CoT terminology, corrects wording such as 'For clarify' to 'For clarity,' and changes several 'Appendix' references to 'Section.' It adds the related-work passage and replaces the preprint footer with NeurIPS 2025 information; the narrative structure is retained.

P2.justification: Figure 2 moves from page 6 to page 7, alongside Figure 3, and text, captions, and other displays undergo modest reflow. All seven figures and five tables are retained without substantive visual redesign.

improvement.justification: Compared with v2, Section 1.1 provides useful context about a closely related continuous-CoT theory paper and explains the contribution's distinction. Small language corrections also improve readability. These are limited gains; the theoretical and empirical substance, including appendix evidence, remains unchanged.
